sentences.text:
Amiya Kumar Bairi And Ors vs The State Of West Bengal And
Ors on 25 August, 2020

Author: Subhasis Dasgupta
Bench: Subhasis Dasgupta
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction
 Original Side
 Wp 214 Of 2020
 With
 Ga 927 of 2020
 Amiya Kumar Bairi And Ors
 Versus
 The State Of West Bengal And Ors.
 Before:
 The Hon'ble Chief Justice Thottathil B. Radhakrishnan
The Hon'ble Justice Subhasis Dasgupta Date : 25th August, 2020.

(Via Video Conference) Mr. Anjan Bhattacharya, Advocate ...for petitioners Mr. Amitesh Banerjee,
Sr. Advocate ...for State.

The Court :- Heard Mr. Anjan Bhattacharya, learned counsel for petitioners and Mr. Amitesh
Banerjee, learned Sr. Advocate for State.
2.  This writ petition, styled as a public interest litigation, is essentially one which could at the best be treated as a representative litigation.
It is filed by persons who claim to be potato farmers or traders dealing in potatoes in the State of West Bengal.
What is attempted to be projected is a collective and similar cause.

Hence this could be considered only as a representative litigation, at the best, and not as a public interest litigation; more particularly because, the petitioners themselves have personal interest in the issue being raised.
3. Be that as it may, we have considered the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners as also for the learned counsel for the State Government.
4. The issue is as to whether it was appropriate for the State to have imposed restrictions on the use of 'Ala Mati' in potatoes.

According to the petitioners 'Ala Mati' is traditionally used in Bengal and few some other sister States to preserve the potatoes and also to give the glaze and polish, which 'Ala Mati' brings to the surface of the potatoes.

The question, fundamentally, therefore, relates to the Amiya Kumar Bairi And Ors vs The State Of West Bengal And Ors on 25 August, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32847291/
1 matters that would fall for concern touching food safety and standards.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Annexure P-1 dated 4th October, 2019 issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India conclude by saying that the use of 'Ala Mati' or 'Yellow Ochre' is not permitted for sprinkling on potatoes.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The discussion of that institution leading to such conclusion is available in the first paragraph of that communication.

The scientific panel on food and vegetables and their products, had opined that 'Ala Mati' is a form of external organic soil dust coating on potato that normally masks the undesirable effects on sprouting or bruising in potatoes and that there is no research data on the effect of 'Ala Mati' or 'Yellow Ochre' on storage life and quality of potatoes.

However, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has also considered that the scientific panel also raised concern related to chance of mixing of chemicals such as anti sprouting agent, inorganic colouring matter, synthetic food colours or pigment along with 'Ala Mati' soil in uncontrollable manner.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
We can safely visualise that what has been done through the decision of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India is to maintain a nice balance between the larger public interest to ensure that consumable food products,
including potatoes, are not subjected to any contamination by adulteration or addition or use of materials, including preservatives, which may not be conducive to health.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Obviously, though the interest of the farmers and those dealing with potatoes in trade and market is also not to be ignored,
that cannot over-ride the larger public need to sustain exclusion of materials which are not fit for human consumption.

When the State Government has acted on the aforesaid material and has issued a further order which is nothing but in tandem with the decision of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, we do not think that it will be within our domain to issue any omnibus protective or pre-emptive order against raid, search, seizure, arrest or in any other manner forking the due process of law.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It would also not be advisable to pass any order which may tend to be one amounting to giving a blanket protection for all persons in an anticipatory form against any proceedings under the penal and other laws.
5. In the aforesaid circumstances, we record the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners that it is for the competent authority in the State Government to consider such issues.

As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the State, it will not be appropriate for the State to issue any order or guideline contrasting the contents of the decision taken and advised by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 6. For the aforesaid reasons, we do not find any ground to entertain this matter and issue any direction.

7. We accordingly dismiss the writ petition preserving the right of any person who may be aggrieved by any action taken by the Government authorities and seek redressal from appropriate jurisdiction in accordance with law.
8. Accordingly the writ petition is dismissed.
So also, GA 927 of 2020.

(THOTTATHIL B. RADHAKRISHNAN, C.J.) (SUBHASIS DASGUPTA, J.)

When the State Government has acted on the aforesaid material and has issued a further order which is nothing but in tandem with the decision of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, we do not think that it will be within our domain to issue any omnibus protective or pre-emptive order against raid, search, seizure, arrest or in any other manner forking the due process of law.
